panels.rationale: Whole-figure plate of 3 panels (Left Panel, Middle Panel, Right Panel). Left Panel: This panel shows the initial positioning of the hand and wrist for the diagnostic Finkelstein's test, a standard finding/maneuver associated with de Quervain tenosynovitis. Middle Panel: The middle panel shows the execution of the Finkelstein's test, which is a key clinical finding used to diagnose de Quervain tenosynovitis. Right Panel: This panel shows the completion of the Finkelstein's test demonstration, which is a classic clinical presentation used to diagnose de Quervain tenosynovitis.

in_text_mentions: disorder characterized by radial-sided wrist pain. Incidence is 10 times higher in women than men and is often associated with overexertion or repetitive movements [1]. It is diagnosed by a history of radial-sided wrist pain and pertinent physical examination findings which include first dorsal compartment tenderness and positive Finkelstein and Eichhoff maneuvers (Figure 1). Neurovascular exam should be normal [2]. A single corticosteroid injection provides complete resolution of symptoms in more than 75% of patients, with few patients requiring a second injection or surgical release [1, 2].
